facts: Capacitance is the ratio of stored charge to potential difference for a conductor or capacitor.
A capacitor stores energy in the electric field between its conductors.
For a parallel-plate capacitor, increasing plate area increases capacitance and increasing separation decreases capacitance.

keyTerms.df: Capacitance is the ratio of stored charge to potential difference for a conductor or capacitor.
keyTerms.eg: For a parallel-plate capacitor, increased plate area provides a concrete case of increased capacitance.
keyTerms.mi: Capacitance is the energy stored between a capacitor's conductors.
keyTerms.cx: Energy is stored in the electric field, whereas capacitance compares stored charge with potential difference.

keyTerms.df: Plate area is a parallel-plate capacitor property whose increase is associated with increased capacitance.
keyTerms.eg: Comparing increased plate area with increased separation distinguishes their opposite relations to capacitance.
keyTerms.mi: Increasing plate area decreases the capacitance of a parallel-plate capacitor.
keyTerms.cx: Greater plate area corresponds to greater capacitance, not decreased capacitance.

keyTerms.df: Separation is a parallel-plate capacitor property whose increase is associated with decreased capacitance.
keyTerms.eg: A parallel-plate comparison can contrast increased separation with increased plate area when labeling capacitance changes.
keyTerms.mi: Increasing separation increases the capacitance of a parallel-plate capacitor.
keyTerms.cx: Greater separation corresponds to lower capacitance, reversing that proposed relationship.

scenario.su: A workshop team must label the capacitance direction for two parallel-plate capacitor designs before a deadline. One design records increasing plate area, while the other records increasing separation, so the team must assign opposite labels from these observations.
scenario.ma: plate-area design notation, separation design notation, capacitance-direction labels

mc.q: A review note compares capacitance based on stored charge and potential difference with energy stored in the electric field between conductors. Which distinction matches these observations?
op: Capacitance ratios charge to potential difference; energy is field-stored
Capacitance is field-stored; energy ratios charge to potential difference
Capacitance is stored charge; energy is field-stored
Capacitance is potential difference; energy is field-stored
mc.ex: Capacitance compares stored charge with potential difference, while a capacitor stores energy in the electric field between its conductors. Stored charge alone is not capacitance because potential difference is also part of the ratio.

mc.q: A parallel-plate capacitor review compares an increased plate area notation with an increased separation notation, while requiring an increased-capacitance label. Which recorded relation supports that label?
op: Increasing plate area increases capacitance
Increasing separation increases capacitance
Increasing plate area decreases capacitance
Decreasing separation decreases capacitance
mc.ex: Increasing plate area increases the capacitance of a parallel-plate capacitor. Increasing separation does not support that label because it decreases capacitance.

facts: Rigid lithospheric plates move above mantle rock that remains solid yet can flow slowly, while heat transfer sustains mantle convection.
Upward mantle flow at ocean ridges helps form new lithosphere while plates diverge.
At convergent boundaries, one plate can be subducted into the mantle beneath another.

keyTerms.df: Mantle convection is heat-sustained movement associated with slowly flowing solid mantle rock.
keyTerms.eg: Heat transfer sustains mantle convection as solid mantle rock flows slowly.
keyTerms.mi: Mantle convection requires mantle rock to stop being solid.
keyTerms.cx: Loss of solidity is not required because the mantle rock can move slowly in its solid state.

keyTerms.df: Ocean ridges are settings where upward mantle flow helps form new lithosphere as plates diverge.
keyTerms.eg: At ocean ridges, upward mantle flow accompanies diverging plates and new lithosphere formation.
keyTerms.mi: Ocean ridges are settings where one plate is subducted beneath another.
keyTerms.cx: That plate relationship identifies convergent boundaries; ridge observations instead pair upward flow with divergence.

keyTerms.df: Convergent boundaries are settings where one plate can descend into the mantle beneath another plate.
keyTerms.eg: One plate is subducted beneath another at convergent boundaries.
keyTerms.mi: Convergent boundaries are where upward mantle flow helps form new lithosphere while plates diverge.
keyTerms.cx: Those observations belong to ocean ridges; convergence is associated with one plate entering the mantle beneath another.

scenario.su: A geology mapper must classify two boundary passages before a deadline, but each passage can receive only one supplied label. One passage records upward mantle flow with diverging plates and new lithosphere, while the other records one plate entering the mantle beneath another.
scenario.ma: ocean-ridge passage recording upward mantle flow, new-lithosphere notation paired with diverging plates, convergent-boundary passage recording one plate beneath another

mc.q: Which distinction fits a comparison between solid mantle rock flowing slowly beneath moving lithospheric plates and upward mantle flow where plates diverge at ocean ridges?
op: Slow solid flow; convergence forms lithosphere
Ridge flow subducts one plate beneath another
Rigid plates flow slowly; mantle plates move
Slow solid flow; ridge flow forms lithosphere
mc.ex: Mantle rock remains solid yet can flow slowly beneath moving lithospheric plates, whereas upward flow at ocean ridges helps form new lithosphere during divergence. Convergence instead permits one plate to be subducted beneath another.

mc.q: A boundary description records upward mantle flow, diverging plates, and new lithosphere, but the student must choose one supported classification before the deadline. Which classification fits?

Convergent boundary with new lithosphere forming
Convergent boundary with plates diverging
Ocean ridge with new lithosphere forming
mc.ex: Upward mantle flow at ocean ridges helps form new lithosphere while plates diverge. A convergent boundary instead can involve one plate being subducted beneath another.

facts: Human anatomy and physiology organizes body structure from chemical components to cells, tissues, organs, organ systems, and the organism, so students can connect form to function across scales.
A cell is the smallest independently functioning unit of a living organism.
Organs are anatomically distinct structures made of two or more tissue types.

keyTerms.df: A cell is the smallest independently functioning unit of a living organism.
keyTerms.eg: A cell represents a unit within body structure.
keyTerms.mi: A cell is made of two or more tissue types.
keyTerms.cx: The independently functioning unit is the cell; the tissue-type description applies to organs.

keyTerms.df: Organs are anatomically distinct body structures composed of two or more tissue types.
keyTerms.eg: Organs occur between tissues and organ systems in body structure.
keyTerms.mi: Organs are the smallest independently functioning units of a living organism.
keyTerms.cx: That smallest-unit property belongs to a cell, while organs are structures made of tissue types.

keyTerms.df: Tissue types are components of organs, which are made of two or more of them.
keyTerms.eg: An organ is made of two or more tissue types.
keyTerms.mi: A tissue type is an anatomically distinct organ.
keyTerms.cx: The anatomically distinct structure is the organ, which is made from tissue types.

scenario.su: A student compares a passage describing the smallest independently functioning unit of a living organism with a notation describing an anatomically distinct structure made of two or more tissue types. The student must assign cell and organ labels, but each label must match its described property.
scenario.ma: passage describing the smallest independently functioning unit, notation describing an anatomically distinct structure made of two or more tissue types

mc.q: A comparison describes a cell as independently functioning and an organ as anatomically distinct and made from tissue types. Which distinction matches the supplied descriptions?
op: Organ has tissue types; cell is anatomically distinct
Cell has tissue types; organ functions independently
Cell functions independently; organ has tissue types
Organ functions independently; cell has tissue types
mc.ex: A cell is the smallest independently functioning unit, whereas an organ is anatomically distinct and made of tissue types. Independent functioning therefore describes the cell rather than the organ.

mc.q: A described structure is anatomically distinct and made of two or more tissue types; the label must come from the structural organization sequence. Which label matches the evidence?
op: Classify the structure as cell
Classify the structure as organ
Classify the structure as tissue
Classify the structure as organ system
mc.ex: An anatomically distinct structure made of two or more tissue types is an organ. A tissue type contributes to that structure rather than naming the described structure itself.

facts: Accessibility and usability evaluation combines standards-based conformance checks with observation of representative users completing realistic tasks.
WCAG organizes web accessibility around the principles perceivable, operable, understandable, and robust.
Evaluation with disabled and older users can find barriers that conformance evaluation alone does not reveal.
A usability test observes users attempting to use a product or service while thinking aloud.
A single disabled participant's experience should not be generalized to all people with disabilities.

keyTerms.df: Conformance evaluation involves standards-based checks that can be combined with observation of representative users completing realistic tasks.
keyTerms.eg: Evaluation with disabled and older users can find barriers that conformance evaluation alone does not reveal.
keyTerms.mi: Conformance evaluation observes users thinking aloud while attempting to use a product or service.
keyTerms.cx: A usability test observes users thinking aloud, while accessibility and usability evaluation combines that observation with standards-based conformance checks.

keyTerms.df: WCAG organizes web accessibility around the principles perceivable, operable, understandable, and robust.
keyTerms.eg: Web accessibility is organized by WCAG as perceivable, operable, understandable, and robust.
keyTerms.mi: WCAG observes representative users completing realistic tasks while thinking aloud.
keyTerms.cx: WCAG organizes web accessibility principles; a usability test observes users attempting to use a product or service while thinking aloud.

keyTerms.df: Representative users are observed completing realistic tasks as part of accessibility and usability evaluation.
keyTerms.eg: Observation records representative users completing realistic tasks alongside standards-based conformance checks.
keyTerms.mi: A single disabled participant represents all people with disabilities.
keyTerms.cx: A single disabled participant's experience should not be generalized to all people with disabilities.

scenario.su: An evaluator must classify records from accessibility and usability evaluation before a deadline. The records show standards-based conformance checks, disabled and older users completing realistic tasks, and users thinking aloud while attempting to use a product or service, but the deadline requires a defensible distinction.
scenario.ma: standards-based conformance-check record, notes of disabled and older users completing realistic tasks, thinking-aloud usability-test observation

mc.q: Conformance evaluation records standards-based checks, while observation shows disabled and older users completing realistic tasks; which evaluation description accounts for the documented comparison?
op: Generalize a disabled participant's experience
Combine conformance checks with representative-user observation
Organize barriers as WCAG principles
Use conformance evaluation to observe representative users
mc.ex: Accessibility and usability evaluation combines standards-based conformance checks with observation of representative users, and evaluation with disabled and older users can reveal barriers missed by conformance evaluation alone. Conformance evaluation is not the thinking-aloud observation of representative users.

mc.q: Users are observed attempting to use a product or service while thinking aloud, and a deadline requires the evaluator to classify this recorded activity; which label is supported?
op: Classify it as a usability test
Generalize it to people with disabilities
Classify it as conformance checks
Classify it as WCAG principles
mc.ex: A usability test observes users attempting to use a product or service while thinking aloud. Standards-based conformance checks belong to the combined evaluation description rather than labeling this observed activity.

facts: Journey mapping represents an end-to-end experience from the user's perspective so a team can see connected steps, boundaries, breakdowns, and opportunities.
A journey map should start from research about the steps users actually take and the transactions involved.
An experience map should make struggle points and candidate improvement areas visible.
A map can reveal dead ends where the user cannot continue toward the larger goal.
Journey analysis should include gaps between online and offline parts of a service.

keyTerms.df: Journey mapping represents an end-to-end experience from the user's perspective.
keyTerms.eg: Journey mapping shows connected steps, boundaries, breakdowns, and opportunities.
keyTerms.mi: Journey mapping represents transactions from the team's perspective.
keyTerms.cx: The represented experience is viewed from the user's perspective.

keyTerms.df: An experience map is distinguished by visible struggle points and candidate improvement areas.
keyTerms.eg: An experience map makes a struggle point and a candidate improvement area visible.
keyTerms.mi: An experience map should make transactions and connected steps visible.
keyTerms.cx: Its stated visible elements are struggle points and candidate improvement areas.

keyTerms.df: Dead ends are points where the user cannot continue toward the larger goal.
keyTerms.eg: A map shows a dead end between connected steps toward the larger goal.
keyTerms.mi: Dead ends are opportunities where the user continues toward the larger goal.
keyTerms.cx: At a dead end, the user cannot continue toward that goal.

scenario.su: A team must classify what its map needs to show before a deadline. The research record includes actual user steps and transactions, while the service review notes a dead end and a gap between online and offline parts.
scenario.ma: research record of actual user steps, transaction record, dead-end notation toward the larger goal, service-review observation of an online-offline gap

mc.q: One map draft begins with researched user steps and transactions, while another highlights struggle points and candidate improvement areas; which distinction matches these observations?
op: Journey map struggle points; experience map research
Journey map steps; experience map improvement areas
Journey map research; experience map transactions
Journey map research; experience map struggle points
mc.ex: A journey map starts from research about actual user steps and transactions, while an experience map makes struggle points and candidate improvement areas visible. Assigning struggle points to the journey map and research to the experience map reverses those relations.

mc.q: Under a deadline, a service review records a blocked continuation toward the larger goal and a gap between online and offline parts; what should journey analysis include?
op: Mark dead end and connected steps
Mark dead end and online-offline gap
Mark online and offline parts
Mark opportunity and online-offline gap
mc.ex: The blocked continuation is a dead end, and journey analysis includes gaps between online and offline service parts. Connected steps do not replace the recorded online-offline gap.

facts: Price elasticity of demand is the percentage change in quantity demanded divided by the percentage change in price.

facts: Gauss's law relates the net electric flux through a closed surface to the net charge enclosed by that surface.
A Gaussian surface is useful for calculating fields when symmetry makes the field magnitude or direction simple on the surface.
Zero enclosed charge implies zero net flux, not necessarily zero electric field everywhere on the surface.

keyTerms.df: Net electric flux is the quantity through a closed surface that Gauss's law relates to the net charge enclosed.
keyTerms.eg: A closed surface with zero enclosed charge has zero net electric flux.
keyTerms.mi: Zero net electric flux means the electric field is zero everywhere on the surface.
keyTerms.cx: A vanishing total flux does not require the field to vanish at every surface location.

keyTerms.df: A Gaussian surface belongs to a field-calculation setting where symmetry can simplify field magnitude or direction.
keyTerms.eg: Symmetry makes the field direction simple on a Gaussian surface used for calculating fields.
keyTerms.mi: A Gaussian surface is useful when its field magnitude and direction are not simple.
keyTerms.cx: Its stated usefulness arises when symmetry simplifies at least one of those field properties.

keyTerms.df: Enclosed charge is the net charge within the closed surface in the relation expressed by Gauss's law.
keyTerms.eg: Zero enclosed charge on a closed surface implies zero net flux through it.
keyTerms.mi: Zero enclosed charge guarantees zero electric field everywhere on the closed surface.
keyTerms.cx: That charge condition determines net flux but does not force every surface field value to vanish.

scenario.su: A student reviews a closed-surface notation showing zero enclosed charge and an observation showing a nonzero electric field at one point on the surface. Before a deadline, the student must label the warranted conclusion while distinguishing net flux from electric field everywhere.

Zero net flux implies nonzero enclosed charge
mc.ex: Zero enclosed charge implies zero net flux without requiring zero electric field everywhere on the surface. Therefore, zero net flux does not require the surface field to vanish.

facts: By the law of supply, a higher price raises the quantity producers are willing to supply, so the supply curve slopes upward.
A change in the good's own price moves along the supply curve, while a change in input costs or technology shifts the whole curve.
Quantity supplied is a flow per period, not a fixed stock.

keyTerms.df: A supply curve has an upward slope relating higher price to greater quantity producers are willing to supply.
keyTerms.eg: A higher price and greater quantity supplied trace the supply curve.
keyTerms.mi: A change in input costs moves the observation along the supply curve.
keyTerms.cx: Input costs shift the whole curve rather than producing movement along it.

keyTerms.df: The good's own price is the price whose change produces movement along the supply curve.
keyTerms.eg: Higher own price is recorded beside greater quantity producers are willing to supply.
keyTerms.mi: A technology change should be classified as an own-price movement.
keyTerms.cx: Technology belongs with changes that shift the whole curve.

keyTerms.df: Quantity supplied is a flow measured per period rather than a fixed stock.
keyTerms.eg: Producers record quantity supplied per period when price is higher.
keyTerms.mi: Quantity supplied identifies a fixed stock available to producers.
keyTerms.cx: It must be treated as a per-period flow instead of a stock.

scenario.su: A producer brief records a change in the good's own price and a change in technology, but the analyst must classify each before a deadline. scenario.ma: the own-price change notation, the technology change record, the movement-along-curve label, the whole-curve-shift label

Both move along the supply curve

Technology moves along; own price shifts curve
mc.ex: A change in the good's own price moves along the supply curve, while technology shifts the whole curve. Technology therefore should not be classified as movement along the curve.

facts: Major and natural minor scales are distinguished by their ordered patterns of whole steps and half steps between adjacent scale degrees.
The major-scale step pattern is whole, whole, half, whole, whole, whole, half.
Natural minor has a whole step from its seventh degree to the tonic, so that degree is called the subtonic.

keyTerms.df: Ordered patterns distinguish major and natural minor scales through the sequence of steps between adjacent scale degrees.
keyTerms.eg: For major, inspect the sequence whole, whole, half, whole, whole, whole, half.
keyTerms.mi: Changing the order of whole steps and half steps leaves the scale distinction intact.
keyTerms.cx: The sequence matters because major and natural minor are distinguished by how those steps are ordered.

keyTerms.df: The major-scale step pattern is an ordered sequence of whole and half steps between adjacent scale degrees.
keyTerms.eg: In the major-scale pattern, a half step follows the first two whole steps.
keyTerms.mi: The major-scale sequence begins whole, half, whole.
keyTerms.cx: Its opening three steps are whole, whole, half.

keyTerms.df: The subtonic is natural minor's seventh degree when that degree is a whole step from the tonic.
keyTerms.eg: When notation shows that whole-step relation, write subtonic beside the seventh degree.
keyTerms.mi: Subtonic names the tonic at the end of the whole step.
keyTerms.cx: The label belongs to natural minor's seventh degree, not the tonic.

scenario.su: An editor must classify two scale notations before a deadline, using their ordered whole-step and half-step details. One notation displays the stated major sequence, while the other displays a whole step from natural minor's seventh degree to the tonic, and each must receive a defensible label.
scenario.ma: major-scale notation: whole, whole, half, whole, whole, whole, half, natural-minor notation: whole step from seventh degree to tonic, proposed label: subtonic for the seventh degree

mc.q: Two scale notations are compared: one shows the stated major sequence, while the other is evaluated by adjacent whole and half steps. Which conclusion makes the defensible distinction?
op: Ordered step patterns distinguish; major reverses stated sequence
Ordered step patterns distinguish; major omits one half step
Ordered step patterns distinguish; major matches stated sequence
Scale degrees distinguish; major matches stated sequence
mc.ex: Major and natural minor are distinguished by ordered step patterns, and the observed major notation matches whole, whole, half, whole, whole, whole, half. The major sequence is stated in that order, not its reverse.

mc.q: A natural minor notation shows a whole step from its seventh degree to the tonic, but the editor may apply just one supported label before the deadline. What should the editor do?
op: Label the whole step as the subtonic
Label the seventh degree as the tonic
Label the seventh degree as the subtonic
Label the tonic as the subtonic
mc.ex: In natural minor, a seventh degree lying a whole step from the tonic is called the subtonic. The tonic does not receive that label; the seventh degree does.

facts: File I/O lets a program read information from and write information into files; a file is accessed by opening it, working with its contents, and closing it.
open() returns a file object that the program then reads from or writes to.
read() reads the entire contents of a file and returns a single string.
readline() returns the next single line, while readlines() returns a list with every line of the file.

keyTerms.df: A file object is what open() returns for a program to read from or write to.
keyTerms.eg: open() returns a file object that the program reads from.
keyTerms.mi: read() returns the file object produced by open().
keyTerms.cx: Instead, open() returns the file object, and read() returns a single string.

keyTerms.df: read() is a file operation that returns the entire contents as a single string.
keyTerms.eg: read() reads the entire contents of a file.
keyTerms.mi: read() returns the next single line from a file.
keyTerms.cx: The next single line comes from readline(); read() returns the entire contents.

keyTerms.df: readlines() is a file operation whose result is a list with every line of the file.
keyTerms.eg: readlines() returns a list with every line of the file.
keyTerms.mi: readlines() returns a single string containing the entire contents.
keyTerms.cx: Its result is a list with every line, whereas read() returns a single string.

scenario.su: A programmer reviews results from read(), readline(), and readlines() after opening a file. The programmer must label each result while preserving the distinction among the entire contents, the next single line, and a list with every line.
scenario.ma: read() notation paired with a single string containing the entire contents, readline() notation paired with the next single line, readlines() notation paired with a list containing every line

mc.q: When comparing observed results, read() produces a single string holding the entire contents, while readline() produces the next single line. Which pairing matches these operations?
op: read(): entire contents; readline(): next single line
read(): next single line; readline(): entire contents
read(): every-line list; readline(): entire contents
read(): next single line; readline(): every-line list
mc.ex: read() returns the entire contents as a single string, whereas readline() returns the next single line. Assigning the next single line to read() reverses these supplied relations.

mc.q: A program records the next single line from one operation and a list with every line from another. Which labels correctly classify the observed results?
op: Next single line: readline(); every-line list: readlines()
Next single line: readlines(); every-line list: readline()
Next single line: read(); every-line list: readlines()
Next single line: readline(); every-line list: read()
mc.ex: readline() returns the next single line, while readlines() returns a list with every line. Reversing those labels assigns each operation the other operation's result.

keyTerms.df: Superposition is the relationship placing older layers below younger layers in an undisturbed sedimentary sequence.

keyTerms.df: Cross-cutting distinguishes a disrupting feature as younger than the geological feature it disrupts.

keyTerms.cx: The cutting feature is younger, while the feature it disrupts is older.

scenario.su: A student must label the relative order represented by an undisturbed sedimentary sequence and a feature cutting across another geological feature. The decision must use the observed relationships without assigning numerical ages.
scenario.ma: layer-position observations recording older layers below younger layers, cross-cutting notations recording the disrupting feature and disrupted geological feature

mc.q: An undisturbed sequence shows one layer below another, while a separate feature disrupts a geological feature; which statement correctly distinguishes superposition from cross-cutting?
op: Superposition orders layers; cross-cutting orders disruptions
Superposition orders disruptions; cross-cutting orders layers
Superposition places younger layers below older layers
Cross-cutting makes disrupted features younger
mc.ex: Superposition places older layers below younger layers, whereas cross-cutting places the disrupting feature after the disrupted feature. Superposition does not govern which feature is younger because it disrupts another.

mc.q: An undisturbed sequence has a lower layer and an upper layer, and one feature cuts across both; which oldest-to-youngest order fits the observations without numerical ages?

Oldest to youngest: upper, lower, cutting feature
Oldest to youngest: cutting feature, lower, upper
Oldest to youngest: lower, cutting feature, upper
mc.ex: Superposition makes the lower layer older than the upper layer, and the cutting feature is younger than both disrupted layers. Placing the upper layer first reverses the layer relationship.

facts: A function is a named, reusable block of code defined with def that runs only when it is called; variables created inside it are local to that call.
A function is defined with the def keyword, a name, parentheses, and a colon, with an indented body.
A variable's scope is the part of the program where it can be accessed.
A variable created inside a function has local scope and cannot be accessed outside the function.
A variable created outside any function has global scope and can be accessed anywhere in the program.

keyTerms.df: A function is a named, reusable block of code defined with def that runs when it is called.
keyTerms.eg: A function defined with def, a name, parentheses, and a colon has an indented body.
keyTerms.mi: A function runs when it is defined.
keyTerms.cx: Defining the function does not run it; the function runs when it is called.

keyTerms.df: Scope is the part of the program where a variable can be accessed.
keyTerms.eg: A variable created outside any function has scope anywhere in the program.
keyTerms.mi: Scope identifies when a function is called.
keyTerms.cx: Scope concerns where a variable can be accessed, while calling concerns when a function runs.

keyTerms.df: Local scope is the access property of a variable created inside a function.
keyTerms.eg: A variable created inside a function has local scope during that call.
keyTerms.mi: Local scope belongs to a variable created outside any function.
keyTerms.cx: Creation inside a function gives a variable local scope; creation outside any function gives it global scope.

scenario.su: A reviewer must label two variables by scope before a deadline, using their creation locations as the constraint. One variable is created inside a function, while the other is created outside any function.
scenario.ma: the inside-function variable-creation record, the outside-function variable-creation record, the local-scope notation, the global-scope notation

mc.q: A review compares a variable created inside a function with one created outside any function; which distinction between local scope and global scope is supported?
op: Inside is local; outside is local
Inside is global; outside is local
Inside is local; outside is global
Inside is global; outside is global
mc.ex: Creation inside a function supports local scope, while creation outside any function supports global scope. Assigning global scope inside and local scope outside reverses both supplied relations.

facts: A seventh chord adds a seventh above a triad, and its function depends on its scale degree and its pull within a tonal progression.
The supertonic seventh chord functions as a terminal pre-dominant with a strong pull toward the dominant.
Adding a seventh to the dominant increases the chord's pull toward the tonic.

keyTerms.df: A seventh chord is a chord formed by adding a seventh above a triad.
keyTerms.eg: A seventh above a triad provides a concrete instance of a seventh chord.
keyTerms.mi: Adding the seventh fixes the chord's function regardless of its tonal setting.
keyTerms.cx: Scale degree and pull within a tonal progression determine the function instead.

keyTerms.df: The supertonic seventh chord has a terminal pre-dominant function and strongly pulls toward the dominant.
keyTerms.eg: A tonal progression containing this chord presents an instance of strong pull toward the dominant.
keyTerms.mi: The supertonic seventh chord increases the dominant's pull toward the tonic.
keyTerms.cx: That increased tonic pull belongs to adding a seventh to the dominant; the supertonic chord pulls toward the dominant.

keyTerms.df: The dominant is a scale degree whose chord gains greater tonic pull when a seventh is added.
keyTerms.eg: Adding a seventh to the dominant exemplifies an increase in the chord's pull toward the tonic.
keyTerms.mi: Adding a seventh to the dominant creates a terminal pre-dominant that pulls toward the dominant.
keyTerms.cx: The added seventh strengthens movement from the dominant toward the tonic, while the terminal pre-dominant description applies to the supertonic seventh chord.

scenario.su: An analyst must distinguish the functions shown in a tonal progression containing a supertonic seventh chord and a dominant with an added seventh. The classification must account for each recorded scale degree and pull while preserving the different destinations shown.
scenario.ma: supertonic seventh-chord notation, dominant-with-added-seventh notation, scale-degree record, tonal-progression pull observations

mc.q: A tonal progression shows a supertonic seventh chord pulling toward the dominant, while adding a seventh to the dominant strengthens movement toward the tonic; which distinction matches these observations?
op: Supertonic targets dominant; dominant targets tonic
Supertonic targets tonic; dominant targets dominant
Dominant targets supertonic; tonic targets dominant
Supertonic increases tonic pull; dominant is pre-dominant
mc.ex: The supertonic seventh chord pulls toward the dominant, whereas adding a seventh to the dominant increases its pull toward the tonic. The supertonic therefore does not take the tonic-directed relation supplied for the dominant.

Function adds the seventh above the triad
mc.ex: A seventh chord's function depends on its scale degree and its pull within a tonal progression. Scale degree is not presented as depending on function and pull.
